---
title: Export and reporting
description: The read-only SQL reporting views and the CSV or JSON export.
---

There are two ways to get data out: a documented read-only SQL surface for BI and ETL consumers, and
a streamed CSV or JSON export from the admin.

## The reporting views

Each environment schema carries two views.

`reporting_<env>.responses` has one row per submitted response, with answers in a wide JSONB column.

| Column         | Type                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `session_id`   | text                         |
| `form_id`      | text                         |
| `form_version` | integer                      |
| `submitted_at` | timestamptz                  |
| `access_mode`  | `anonymous` or `secure_link` |
| `answers`      | jsonb                        |

`reporting_<env>.answers_flat` is the same data unpivoted to long format, one row per answer, with
`question_id`, `value` and `instance_id`. The instance id is the repeating-group instance the answer
belongs to, or null outside every group.

Values use the canonical encodings: a JSON string for text, a finite number, an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`
string for a date, a JSON boolean, an option id string for single choice, and a deduplicated array
of option ids for multi choice.

A row appears only when its session is submitted and is not erased. Because the exclusion is in the
view definition, no consumer query can accidentally read non-submitted or erased data.

Since workspaces, each workspace gets its own view pair per environment. The unprefixed pair is the
application's and is granted to no consumer.

### Connecting a consumer

Create the role, then grant it:

```sql
CREATE ROLE "qcms_reporting_prod_home" LOGIN PASSWORD '<from-secret-store>';
```

```sh
DATABASE_URL=postgres://qcms_migrate:...@host:5432/qcms \
  pnpm qcms:environment reporting
```

That creates or replaces one view set per workspace and environment pair, and grants each pair's
role usage on its own reporting schema and select on exactly its own two views. It is idempotent, so
run it after creating a workspace.

Additive changes to the views are a minor version; renames and removals are major. Column order is
not part of the promise, so select columns by name.

## The HTTP export

```sh
curl -s "$API/admin/forms/frm_auto_quote/export?format=csv&version=1" \
  -H "x-qcms-internal-token: $INT" -H "x-qcms-admin-session: $ADM"
```

```sh
curl -s "$API/admin/forms/frm_auto_quote/export?format=json" \
  -H "x-qcms-internal-token: $INT" -H "x-qcms-admin-session: $ADM"
```

Parameters are `format` (`csv` or `json`), `shape` (`long` or `wide`), `version`, `from` and `to`.
The export is streamed.

JSON may span versions and is an array of `{ sessionId, formId, formVersion, submittedAt, accessMode, answers }`.

### CSV rules

A `version` is required for CSV, because the column set depends on it. The columns are the metadata
columns `session_id`, `form_version`, `submitted_at` and `access_mode`, then one column per question
of that version's form, in document order.

- Multi choice serializes as option ids joined by `;`.
- RFC 4180 quoting: a field is quoted when it contains a comma, a double quote, CR or LF, and
  embedded quotes are doubled. Records end with CRLF.
- A UTF-8 byte-order mark is prefixed once.
- An unanswered question is an empty cell.

### The two shapes

`shape=long` is the default. One file carries the metadata columns and every question outside a
group, plus one file per group at the group's own grain, with `session_id`, `instance_ordinal`,
`instance_id` and the member questions. A version with at least one group answers a zip of those
files; a version with none answers a single CSV.

`shape=wide` folds each group's member questions back into one flat file as indexed columns. Be
careful: a group whose maximum is 500 produces 500 columns per member question, whether any session
filled two of them or none.

## Other data-out routes

`GET /admin/forms/:id/responses` lists submitted responses with paging and filters.
`GET /admin/forms/:id/responses/:sessionId` reads one response: the locked answers, the append-only
answer ledger, and the content hash.

## Retention

Two sweeps keep the ledger from growing without bound. Abandoned sessions past their expiry move to
expired, keeping the ledger row. An optional hard cleanup permanently removes the ledger rows for
sessions that expired and were never submitted; it never touches submitted content or erased
sessions.

:::note
Scheduled or automated exports are out of scope. There is no public read API for responses: the
machine paths are the SQL views and this internal admin endpoint, which carries no stability
contract.
:::
